title: City & country prepositions
subtitle: à / en / au / aux / de — pick the right one before each place name.
blurb: Pretest yourself on place prepositions before the speed-drill.

items.contextLabel: [Plotting itinerary] Telling someone where you live
items.why: à Paris — cities always take à, regardless of gender. en is for countries and regions; au is for masculine countries; dans is used with dans le centre de Paris (inside a part of), not for the city name itself.

whyWrong.en: en is for countries and regions — Paris is a city: à.
whyWrong.au: au is for masculine countries (au Japon) — cities take à.
whyWrong.dans: dans works for parts of a city (dans le centre de Paris), not the city name.

items.fullSentence: Elle étudie en France cette année.
items.sentenceTrans: She is studying in France this year.
items.why: en France — France is feminine (ends in -e), so the location preposition is en. The same applies to en Espagne, en Italie, en Chine, en Allemagne — all feminine because they end in -e. à is for cities, not countries; dans la France exists but means a very specific subregion.

whyWrong.à: à is for cities — France is a feminine country: en.
whyWrong.au: au is for masculine countries — France is feminine: en.
whyWrong.dans la: dans la France would mean a specific subregion — the rule is en France.

items.contextLabel: [Plotting itinerary] A colleague on a business trip
items.fullSentence: Il est en voyage au Japon.
items.sentenceTrans: He is on a business trip in Japan.
items.why: au Japon — Japon is masculine (does not end in -e), so use au (= à + le). Other masculine countries: le Canada → au Canada, le Maroc → au Maroc, le Portugal → au Portugal. en would only be correct for feminine countries.

whyWrong.en: en is for feminine countries — Japon is masculine: au.
whyWrong.à: à is for cities — Japon is a country.
whyWrong.dans le: dans le Japon isn't used for being in a country — au Japon.

items.fullSentence: On va aux États-Unis cet été.
items.sentenceTrans: We're going to the United States this summer.
items.why: aux États-Unis — plural country names take aux (= à + les). les Pays-Bas → aux Pays-Bas; les Philippines → aux Philippines. à les does not exist in French — it always contracts to aux. au is singular masculine only.

whyWrong.au: au is singular masculine — États-Unis is plural: aux.
whyWrong.en: en is for feminine countries — les États-Unis is plural: aux.
whyWrong.à les: à les doesn't exist — it always contracts to aux.

items.contextLabel: [Plotting itinerary] Telling where you are from
items.why: de Singapour — for origin from a city, use de (or d' before a vowel). d' would be used before a vowel: je viens d'Oslo, d'Amsterdam. du is for masculine countries (je viens du Japon). depuis means 'since' (time) or 'from' (direction of movement), not origin.

whyWrong.d': d' is only before a vowel — Singapour starts with S.
whyWrong.du: du is for masculine countries (du Japon) — cities take plain de.

items.contextLabel: [Plotting itinerary] Meeting someone at a conference
items.why: d'Oslo — de elides to d' before a vowel or silent h. City names starting with a vowel: d'Amsterdam, d'Athènes, d'Oslo, d'Istanbul, d'Édimbourg. This is mandatory elision — de Oslo is not acceptable. The rule applies to any place name, not just cities.

whyWrong.de: Oslo starts with a vowel — de elides to d'.
whyWrong.du: du is for masculine countries — cities take de/d'.
whyWrong.des: des is for plural names (des États-Unis).

items.why: de France — for feminine countries as origin, use de alone (no article). NOT de la France. This is a fixed rule: je viens de France, d'Espagne, de Chine, d'Italie. The article disappears entirely with country names in origin constructions.

whyWrong.de la: for origin the article drops with feminine countries: de France, not de la France.
whyWrong.du: du is for masculine countries (du Japon) — France is feminine: de.
whyWrong.d'en: d'en isn't a French combination here.

items.why: du Japon — masculine countries keep their article in origin constructions: du (= de + le). Contrast with feminine countries: de France (no article). Masculine: je viens du Canada, du Maroc, du Portugal, du Mexique. The article only disappears with feminine country names.

whyWrong.de: masculine countries keep their article for origin: du Japon, not de Japon.
whyWrong.d': Japon starts with a consonant, and masculine countries need du anyway.
whyWrong.des: des is for plural countries (des États-Unis) — le Japon is masculine singular: du.

items.fullSentence: Il fait son stage en Afrique.
items.sentenceTrans: He is doing his internship in Africa.
items.why: en Afrique — continents follow the same rule as feminine countries: en (Europe, Asie, Afrique, Amérique du Sud are all feminine). en Europe, en Asie, en Afrique, en Amérique. à l' is used for the article form of names (à l'est de), not for the continent name itself. au is masculine singular only.

whyWrong.au: au is masculine singular — continents are feminine: en.
whyWrong.à l': à l' isn't used with continent names — en Afrique.
whyWrong.dans l': dans l' isn't the continent rule — en Afrique.

items.fullSentence: On réserve un hôtel au Mexique.
items.sentenceTrans: We're booking a hotel in Mexico.
items.why: au Mexique — le Mexique ends in -e but is masculine (an exception to the '-e = feminine' rule). So it takes au, not en. Other notable masculine -e countries: le Mozambique (au Mozambique), le Cambodge (au Cambodge), le Zimbabwe (au Zimbabwe). When in doubt, look up the article; the rule is a strong tendency, not a law.

whyWrong.en: Mexique ends in -e but is masculine (an exception) — au Mexique.
whyWrong.à: à is for cities — Mexique is a country.
whyWrong.dans le: dans le Mexique isn't used — au Mexique.

items.why: en Inde — countries starting with a vowel take en, even the masculine ones: en Inde, en Iran, en Irak. (And their origin form elides: d'Inde, never de l'Inde.) The article you know from l'Inde disappears after the preposition.

whyWrong.à l': à l' is for places (à l'école) — country names drop the article: en Inde.
whyWrong.au: au is for masculine consonant-initial countries (au Japon) — vowel-initial ones take en.
whyWrong.dans l': dans l' isn't used for being in a country — en Inde.

items.contextLabel: [Plotting itinerary] Asking where someone is from
items.sentenceTrans: She comes from the United States.
items.why: des États-Unis — plural country names use des (= de + les) for origin. de les never exists — it always contracts to des. du is for masculine singular countries (du Japon), and bare de drops the article, which plural country names keep.

whyWrong.du: du is masculine singular (du Japon) — plural country names take des.
whyWrong.de les: de les doesn't exist — it contracts to des.
whyWrong.de: plural country names keep the article: des États-Unis.

recap.example: à Paris, à Tokyo, à Londres
en France, en Espagne, en Chine
en Europe, en Asie, en Afrique
au Japon, au Canada, au Maroc
du Japon, du Canada, du Maroc

recap.note: à = at (time) — same preposition, different use
